frozen_problem.title: Flat strips, counting conventions, and a width bound
frozen_problem.statement:
Question 6.1.1. If we assume that the curvature is only C0, then a metric with such a geodesic can be constructed. Each end of the geodesic is asymptotic to a closed geodesic. But a geodesic along which the curvature is zero cannot spiral into a closed geodesic if the curvature is C2; see [Ruggiero1998]. Wu [Wu2013] has recently given a negative answer to the question under the assumption that the subset of the surface where the curvature is negative has finitely many components; he also shows under this hypothesis that only finitely many free homotopy classes can contain zero curvature closed geodesics. 14 KEITH BURNS AND VLADIMIR S. MATVEEV

A flat strip is a totally geodesic isometric immersion of the Riemannian product of R with an interval. Zero curvature geodesics can be viewed as flat strips with infinitesimal width. It is known that all flat strips (with positive width) must close up in the R-direction; in other words they are really immersions of the product of S1 with an interval. Furthermore for each δ > 0 there are only finitely many flat strips with width ≥ δ. Proofs can be found in a preprint of Cao and Xavier [Cao-Xav]. The main idea is that if two flat strips of width δ cross each other at a very shallow angle, then their intersection contains a long rectangle with width close to 2 δ.It is possible that there are only finitely many flat strips. This is true when the set where the curvature is negative has finitely many components [Wu2013], but the only effort to prove it in general [Rodriguez Hertz2003] was unsuccessful.

theory.target: Falsify corner-plus-center sampling for a nonconvex strip union, and certify an exact all-points containment criterion for arbitrary translated axis-aligned rectangles, including its sharp normalized height-versus-length frontier.
definitions: U is the union of the closed normalized bands |X+Y|<=1 and |Y-X|<=1.
For all real a<b,c0<d, R=[a,b]x[c0,d]; ell=b-a>0 and H=d-c0>0.
[p,q] and [r,t] are full absolute-value interval images, including zero when the interval crosses it.
Physical X=2sx/delta,Y=2cy/delta with delta,c,s>0 and c^2+s^2=1.
Height is a coordinate dimension; translations are unrestricted, rotations are excluded.
At ell=4, zero height is a degenerate relaxation and is not an admissible positive rectangle.
assumptions: Normalized union U={|X+Y|<=1} union {|Y-X|<=1}; rectangles [a,b]x[c,d] have a<b,c<d.
Physical unit normals are (s,c) and (-s,c), c,s>0 and c^2+s^2=1; X=2*s*x/delta and Y=2*c*y/delta.
Length ell=b-a and height H=d-c are normalized coordinate dimensions, not necessarily the rectangle shorter-side width.
All translations but only coordinate-aligned rectangles are allowed; arbitrary rotations are outside this target.
Boundary equality is allowed because both bands and rectangles are closed. Zero height at ell=4 is degenerate, not a positive rectangle.
No surface development, immersion, maximal-strip counting, area theorem, novelty or parent-solution claim.
approaches_considered: Use corners plus center as a convexity-style certificate; rejected by an exact nonconvex-union counterexample.
Reduce full containment to absolute-coordinate ranges and derive four placement-type upper bounds with attainers.
Independently maximize common slack over four exterior regions via exact rational LPs and reconstruct frontier case maxima.
falsification_targets: Membership at four corners and the center suffices.
The frontier is continuous through ell=2.
A finite coordinate gauge can be imposed without proof.

claims.statement: Corners and center in a union of two strips imply rectangle containment.
claims.falsification_condition: For [-2,2]^2 all five samples pass but (2,0) has violation 1.

claims.statement: For every real axis-aligned rectangle, with absolute-coordinate ranges [p,q],[r,t], containment in the normalized strip union is equivalent to q-r<=1 and t-p<=1. Ordinary universal proof, not independently authored or kernel accepted.
claims.falsification_condition: A failed absolute-range identity, missing coordinate combination or disagreement with original strip forms.

claims.statement: The sharp positive-height frontier is 4-2ell for 0<ell<=1, 2 for 1<=ell<=2, and 2-ell/2 for 2<ell<4; no positive rectangle exists for ell>=4. This is normalized axis-aligned height, not arbitrary-rotation width. Ordinary proof awaits independent review.
claims.falsification_condition: An omitted placement type, unjustified centering/gauge restriction, larger feasible rectangle or invalid attainer.

claims.statement: Two exact algorithms agree on 1296 rectangles and 19 lengths; 200 rectangles are contained and 266 pass corner-plus-center sampling falsely. Seventeen frontier attainers pass original-form LP checks and seven corruptions are rejected.
claims.falsification_condition: An omitted input, differing table entry, false attainer or accepted corruption.
